title: Kollar's lemma: a Noetherian local ring is Artinian, regular of dimension one, of depth at least two, or has a finite birational-type extension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring. Consider the four properties: (1) $R$ is Artinian (every descending chain of ideals of $R$ is stationary); (2) $R$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; (3) $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]; (4) there is a ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$ to a nonzero commutative ring $R'$ such that $R'$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module through $\varphi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $\varphi$ is not an isomorphism, there is an integer $n\ge1$ with $\mathfrak m^n\cdot\ker(\varphi)=0$ and $\mathfrak m^n R'\subseteq\varphi(R)$, and $\mathfrak m$ is not an associated prime of the $R$-module $R'$, i.e. there is no $z\in R'$ whose annihilator $\{a\in R:\varphi(a)z=0\}$ equals $\mathfrak m$. Then (i) at least one of (1)-(4) holds, and (ii) (3) and (4) do not hold together.

proof.text: *Reduction to $R$ not Artinian.* If $R$ is Artinian, (1) holds and (i) is proved. From now on until Step 8 assume $R$ is not Artinian. Then no power of $\mathfrak m$ is zero: if $\mathfrak m^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] with $C=R$ and $K=0$ (indeed $\mathfrak m^N\subseteq0\subseteq\mathfrak m$): $R=R/0$ is Artinian, a contradiction. (The source uses for this the equivalent remark that $V(\mathfrak m)$ is nowhere dense, Proposition 00KJ.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BHZ (lemma-hart-serre-loc-thm, line 28923), proof, first paragraph ('Observe that (R, m) is not Artinian if and only if V(m) is nowhere dense ... We assume this from now on'), lines 28942-28945

proof.text: *The ideal $J$.* Let $J=\{r\in R:\mathfrak m^kr=0\text{ for some }k\ge0\}$, the union of the increasing chain of ideals $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\mathfrak m^k)$, $k\ge0$; it is an ideal, the largest ideal killed by a power of $\mathfrak m$. As $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], the ascending chain $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\mathfrak m^k)$ is stationary (an ascending chain of ideals in a ring all of whose ideals are finitely generated stabilizes: its union is finitely generated, and its finitely many generators lie in one member), so $J=\operatorname{Ann}_R(\mathfrak m^n)$ for some $n\ge1$, i.e. $\mathfrak m^nJ=0$. Moreover $\mathfrak m$ is not an associated prime of $R/J$: if $\bar z\in R/J$, $z\in R$, has $\{a\in R: a\bar z=0\}=\mathfrak m$, then $\mathfrak mz\subseteq J$, so $\mathfrak m^{n+1}z\subseteq\mathfrak m^nJ=0$, hence $z\in J$, $\bar z=0$, whose annihilator is $R\ne\mathfrak m$.

proof.text: *(ii), the kernel.* Suppose $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge2$ and $\varphi:R\to R'$, $n$ are as in (4). As $\mathfrak mR=\mathfrak m\ne R$, clause (1) of [def-weil-pbc-depth] says the supremum of the lengths of $R$-regular sequences in $\mathfrak m$ is $\ge2$, so there is an $R$-regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_r$ in $\mathfrak m$ with $r\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; its first element $f_1\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$. Since $f_1^n\in\mathfrak m^n$ and $\mathfrak m^n\ker\varphi=0$, $f_1^n\ker\varphi=0$, and $f_1^n$ is a nonzerodivisor, so $\ker\varphi=0$.

lean.statement: theorem kollar_local_dichotomy (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] : let extension : Prop := ∃ (S : Type (max u v)) (sRing : CommRing S), letI := sRing ∃ φ : R →+* S, letI := φ.toAlgebra Nontrivial S ∧ Module.Finite R S ∧ ¬ Function.Bijective φ ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ (maximalIdeal R) ^ n * RingHom.ker φ = ⊥ ∧ ∀ z ∈ Ideal.map φ ((maximalIdeal R) ^ n), z ∈ φ.range) ∧ ¬ ∃ z : S, ∀ a : R, φ a * z = 0 ↔ a ∈ maximalIdeal R (IsArtinianRing R ∨ (IsRegularLocalRing R ∧ ringKrullDim R = 1) ∨ (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ depth (R := R) R ∨ extension) ∧ ¬ ((2 : ℕ∞) ≤ depth (R := R) R ∧ extension)
